title: Brighton in talks with Amario Cozier-Duberry over new deal after Bolton loan
content:
Brighton & Hove Albion are in talks with Amario Cozier-Duberry over a new contract.

The south-coast club are keen to keep hold of the former Arsenal winger, who is on a season-long loan with Bolton Wanderers in League One.

Cozier-Duberry’s existing contract runs until June 2028. The 20-year-old is well known to Brighton’s sporting director Jason Ayto, who started out at Arsenal as an academy analyst.

If fresh terms are agreed, a decision will be made in the summer on whether to loan Cozier-Duberry out again or to keep him with Fabian Hurzeler’s first-team squad. The chances of that happening will increase if Brighton qualify for Europe, leading to a more congested fixture list.

Cozier-Duberry is attracting interest from clubs in Germany, Portugal and Belgium, as well as the UK. The right winger, signed by Brighton on a free transfer from Arsenal in the summer transfer window in 2024, has flourished at Bolton after a less successful season on loan to Blackburn Rovers in the Championship in 2024-25.

Cozier-Duberry has scored nine goals in 36 appearances for Bolton this term across all competitions.

He has been in prolific form under former Stoke City manager Steve Schumacher at Bolton, operating as an inverted winger in a 4-2-3-1 system akin to the style head coach Hurzeler uses at Brighton.

Cozier-Duberry’s momentum was interrupted by a knee ligament injury, which kept him out from the end of January, but he has hit the ground running again since his recent return to action. He scored twice on his first game back in the starting line-up in a 5-1 home win against Stevenage last week and has contributed eight goals with ten assists in 32 league appearances overall. Bolton are third in the table and heading for the play-offs.
